_quiz_pool.question: Why do rivers flow downward?
options: Gravity pulls water toward Earth's centre
_quiz_pool.explanation: Gravity pulls water from higher elevations to lower elevations.

_quiz_pool.question: What does g represent in physics?
_quiz_pool.explanation: g is acceleration due to gravity, about 9.81 m/s² on Earth.

_quiz_pool.question: What energy does moving water possess?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Flowing water has kinetic energy of motion.

_quiz_pool.question: What shapes river meanders over time?
options: Moving water energy eroding soil and rock
_quiz_pool.explanation: Flowing water carries kinetic energy that erodes banks and shapes curves.

cover.title: How rivers carve the land
cover.subtitle: Water flowing down valleys holds energy and shapes deserts. Discover how mass, height, and gravity move mountains of rock.
cover.image_caption: The San Juan River in Utah
cover.subject: Physics · Energy
cover.fun_fact: A cubic metre of water weighs one thousand kilograms and carries huge energy down slopes.
story.title: Curves in the desert
story.lead: Satellite images show the San Juan River carving deep, curvy meanders into the desert landscape in Utah [1]. Flowing water has energy that moves soil and rock over time [1].
stat.1.label: mass of one cubic metre of water in kilograms
stat.2.label: gravitational field strength in metres per second squared
stat.3.label: potential energy in kilojoules for a ten metre drop
story.body_1: Rivers flow from high places to low places because of gravity. As water drops down a valley, it gains speed and kinetic energy. This energy lets rivers cut through rock and carry sand and gravel away [1].
story.body_2: Other satellite images show island landscapes and nighttime lights across continents [2, 3]. Wherever water flows, it obeys strict physics laws of energy and motion [1].
timeline.1.text: Water starts high with stored gravitational potential energy.
timeline.2.text: Water flows down, converting potential energy into kinetic energy.
timeline.3.text: River deposits soil and rock in flatter lowland areas.
physics.title: Gravitational potential energy
physics.body_1: When an object sits high up, it has gravitational potential energy, Ep. The amount depends on mass, gravity, and height.
physics.body_2: In rivers, water high in the mountains has high Ep. As it drops, that energy turns into motion, which erodes riverbeds and carries sediment.
physics.assumptions: We assume gravity is constant and ignore friction losses along the river channel.
example.step_1: Mass m = 1,000 kg, height h = 10 m
table.note: Energy increases directly with height drop.

graph.2.label: 10 m
graph.3.label: 20 m
graph.note: Doubling the height drop doubles the potential energy.
physics.tip: Remember that energy cannot be created or destroyed; gravitational potential energy turns into motion.
